title: My Stone Age racing game is out, where you put your car together from stone, wood and bone
author: SzigetiDev
selftext:
![img](527q3o8j1y3i1 "The garage, where every race starts")

Hi all! I'm Balázs from Hungary, and recently my Stone Age arcade racing game called **Stone Rod** came out for mobile.

The basic idea of the game came from a favorite game of my childhood, Street Rod, just in a totally different "era" :). In the game, before the races, you can build your own Stone Age vehicle in your garage. You choose the body, the drive and the wheels, then if you want, you can add some extras like a roof, a windscreen, etc., to make it even more unique. The parts are made of stone, wood or bone, and every one of them has its own "character".

![img](2cyvg17m1y3i1 "Stone, wood and bone: each has its upsides and downsides")

Building it is not only about looks. The parts have an effect on the car's properties: speed, acceleration, grip, weight and durability. So it's good to think about what you put on the car, because in the race they also change how the car behaves.

For example, if you change the stone wheels to wooden ones, your car will be lighter, but its grip goes down, and the wheels also wear out a lot faster. The stats you see in the garage and the physics system use the same formulas, so if the grip value goes down, you will feel it in the next corner too.

![video](0ktqcazo1y3i1 "Stone to wood: lighter (a higher Weight score means a lighter car), less grip, faster wear")

# How did Tripo get into the picture?

Because I work on it alone, only in my free time, I needed a method to make a lot of 3D models in the same style in a relatively short time.

This is how Tripo came in: an AI-based 3D generator that I already knew from earlier.

First, I tried it for the AI assistant of a web app I developed, where I made 3D heads. I liked the result, so later I started to use it more seriously for another game of mine, *Legend of the DEV*. This is a 2D idle game, where sprites are rendered from the 3D models for fixed scenes.

The models came out so well that I started to think: what if I made a full 3D game with them too?

This is how the idea of Stone Rod was born, this time in Unity.

*Legend of the DEV* will get its own post soon anyway. It's a game about the life of a developer, so it's kind of ironic that I'm writing about it instead of developing it. :)

# From an idea to a 3D model you can use in the game

This is more or less how I make a new 3D model at the moment (a character, a vehicle part or any track element).

As a first step, I write the prompt for the image (or have it written :)). I attach the icon of the game to help the generator with the style. Based on this, I let Tripo's image generation service make the image (usually with the GPT Image 2.5 model). If I have a lot of Tripo credits, then I make more variations at once, so I can choose which one I like the most. Anyway, I really like that we can choose from several image generation models (Nano Banana, Midjourney), so you can even make the same idea with different models and compare which one you like the most. After this, I let Tripo make a 3D model from the chosen image.

![img](o6pc4hyr1y3i1 "Choosing the image model and picking from the versions in Tripo")

But the generated model does not go into the game right away. I have my own Blender script, which does several important post-processing steps automatically; for example, it turns the model to the right direction, scales it to its place, reduces the geometry to a triangle count that also works on mobile, and on the car bodies it marks the connection points where the other parts can go.

When the model is ready, I export it, and it can go into Unity.

About the Blender script and the automated processing, I would like to tell more later, in a separate post.

![img](vnuo7q6u1y3i1 "One model's journey: picture, 3D model, Blender cleanup, game")

# Where is the game now?

Stone Rod can already be downloaded from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6821340705) and [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=hu.stonerod.game). You race against AI opponents, from foggy swamps up to snowy mountain passes, and with the updates, new parts are coming all the time.

![img](v1gi6grx1y3i1 "Racing the rivals on Mammoth Gorge")

Right after the release, I started something new. There is a little dragon in it, and it's already eaten up most of my free time. I'll tell you about it next week.

*The 3D models are made with the help of Tripo:* [*studio.tripo3d.ai*](https://studio.tripo3d.ai)*. The post-processing, the optimization and the Unity integration are the work of my pipeline.*

*This post is sponsored by Tripo.*
